messages:
zoe: Noticed an odd support report: when customers hit the Insights snapshot export, the dashboard preview sometimes shows a KPI from a different org. Customer says it happens after quick role switch.
ben: I can reproduce locally by flipping org in the UI quickly and clicking snapshot/export. Repro ~30%. The exported JSON has a tenant field mismatch (`org_id: org-x` vs request header `x-org: org-y`).
marta: That area shares an in-memory LRU cache in the console service to avoid recomputing panels. We recently changed routing so some internal calls remove the tenant header for path-normalization. Probably a cache-key or header strip bug.
sam: Logs show internal call to /internal/snapshot with cookie-based routing, then snapshot service responds with cached payload. Cache key is currently `snapshot:${panelId}:${range}`. No tenant. Oops.
zoe: Support case: https://support.internal/tickets/INC-4221 (screenshot redacted). They mentioned it surfaced after the rollout of route-affinity changes last week.
ben: Quick mitigation idea: make the snapshot service discard any cached payload whose embedded tenant != incoming tenant header. Add metric `snapshot.cache_tenant_violation` and sampling to capture the offending payload ids (scrub sensitive fields).
marta: We should fix cache key to include tenant tag. Also consider storing tenant-scoped caches (e.g., `tenant:${org}:${key}`) to avoid future cross-tenant collisions.
sam: Agree. Two-step plan: 1) deploy defensive discard+metric (non-breaking) to canary; 2) change cache key and run a backfill purge for suspect keys. For purge: add endpoint `POST /internal/cache/purge?tenant=...&panel=...` and run for affected orgs.
zoe: Can we do a soft-fail mode where we return 412 with a short message and trigger recompute for mismatched tenant so customers see correct content immediately? Might be safer than returning stale wrong data.
ben: I'm in favor of failing-closed (412) on mismatch to avoid leakage. UX team prefers invisible fallback (recompute) rather than error pages. We can recompute on mismatch and also increment the metric.
marta: Also need to check quota enforcement: if recompute bypasses cache it might hit quota checks on the backend and surface rate-limits to customers. Ensure recompute counts against tenant quotas properly.
sam: I'll wire quota token for recompute and ensure request includes `x-org` so quota authz picks it up. Also add a safeguard: if recompute rate > 10/s for an org, circuit-break and throttle to protect downstream.
zoe: Great. For rollout: ASSERTION patch (discard+metric+recompute) to 5% canary, watch `snapshot.cache_tenant_violation` and SLOs (p95 render). If clean for 30m, bump to 25% -> 100% and then deploy cache-key change with staged purge.
marta: Add an integration test in the console harness that simulates cookie flip + rapid panel fetch; should assert no cross-tenant returns.
ben: I'll open PR with tests and the fail-closed behavior. Plan to include a small migration to rename keys to `tenant:${org}:snapshot:${panel}:${range}`.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: service=console-snapshot, route=canary-5%, commit=bb7d2a (tenant-assertion+recompute-fallback).
zoe: I'll notify support and ask affected customer to clear local cache; Ops can run purge for their org if needed.
marta: Postmortem template pre-created. If we see >0 events in prod after rollout, we'll run incident review.
ben: FYI adding a small alert: alert if `snapshot.cache_tenant_violation` > 1/min for >5min. That should catch any regression early.
zoe: Thanks everyone. Filing short incident note and linking to PR once ready.
